title: Bright Toddlers Remember Every Clue, Yet One Moved Marble Stumps Them
description:
Myth vs. Neural Mechanism — Simon Baron-Cohen, Alan Leslie & Uta Frith (1985): The 'Sally-Anne' Marble Transfer & Theory of Mind, grounded in Simon Baron-Cohen, Alan M. Leslie, Uta Frith (1985) (Does the autistic child have a “theory of mind” ? Cognition). Empirical findings show that building on Premack & Woodruff (1978) and Wimmer & Perner's 1983 chocolate story, Simon Baron-Cohen, Alan Leslie, and Uta Frith created the minimalist 'Sally-Anne' tabletop doll test at London's MRC Cognitive Development Unit in 1985.

At the circuit level, this episode examines how parietal cortex, prefrontal cortex coordinate behavioral and neural responses, alongside evidence that the child sits across from two small dolls: Sally (who has a round covered basket) and Anne (who has a rectangular covered box).

Primary Peer-Reviewed Sources:
- Simon Baron-Cohen, Alan M. Leslie, Uta Frith (1985). Does the autistic child have a “theory of mind” ? Cognition. https://doi.org/10.1016/0010-0277(85)90022-8
- Simon Baron-Cohen (2011). Simon Baron-Cohen: I want to banish evil. New Scientist. https://doi.org/10.1016/s0262-4079(11)60809-9
- Jules Morgan (2015). Simon Baron-Cohen: cultivating diversity. The Lancet Psychiatry. https://doi.org/10.1016/s2215-0366(15)00461-7
